name: Email delivery adapter
purpose: Names the narrow interface the auth flow uses to hand a composed sign-in URL to an external email transport, and specifies the outcome shape returned. Provider selection, credential handling, and provider-specific error semantics live inside project-authored implementations of this interface; nothing on the auth routes or the managers reaches around the interface.
responsibilities: Declare the send({ to, subject, textBody, htmlBody }) method as the sole auth-facing surface and { ok, providerStatus, providerMessageId, error } as the sole returned shape (AC-3110-1).
Ship one stub adapter implementation that resolves { ok: true, providerStatus: 200, providerMessageId: 'stub' } and records outgoing calls in memory, for tests and dry runs (AC-3110-3).
Route send failures to the auth event log via an adapterSendFailed entry without changing the POST /login response body or status (AC-3110-2, AC-3109-1).
internalStructure: One JSDoc-typed interface declaration in the contract file and one stub-implementation module; provider adapters (SMTP, Resend, SES) are project-authored modules that satisfy the interface. The routes hold an adapter reference passed at composition time and call adapter.send directly.

interfaces.name: send
interfaces.description: send({ to, subject, textBody, htmlBody }) -> Promise<{ ok, providerStatus, providerMessageId, error }>; the sole method the auth code calls on the adapter.

tradeoffs: Fixing the return shape means every provider adapter has to normalise its own vocabulary (provider status codes, provider message ids) into the four declared fields; that is the cost of keeping the auth code provider-neutral. Projects that need richer provider observability wire it on the provider side of the interface and mirror the salient fields onto the adapterSendFailed event outcome.
